source.display_title: 06/07/2026 - Frank Abt x Ben Byrne  — Closed

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced anywhere on the call. The prospect self-selected after following Trevor since roughly 2021 — 'I've been thinking about it for years.'

prospect.name: Frank Abt
prospect.location: St. Petersburg, Florida, USA (relocated from New Jersey two months earlier)
prospect.occupation: Runs warehouse and operations for a wholesale distribution business in beauty and skincare, supplying US grocery chains, Target, Walmart and Amazon. Desk-bound, 9:30 to 7:00 or 7:30, roughly ten-hour days.
prospect.family_status: Single — came out of a three-year relationship recently. No children. Chocolate labrador puppy called Maple. Describes a 'heavier set family' in which he is the only one in shape; has a sister.
prospect.training_background: Athlete through high school and college, then ten to fifteen years of a bodybuilding 'bro split' — one body part a day — which he says has not changed in a decade. Was visibly shredded with a six-pack at peak, roughly five years ago. Since then a cycle of three-to-four-month bursts followed by relapse, including stretches of six months with no gym at all. Tracks macros in MyFitnessPal, has done weekly photo and food check-ins with a friend who is a natural bodybuilder and who coached him to his best condition. Currently doing yoga once a week, morning stretching and Qigong-derived mobility work learned from his ex-partner, and lunchtime walks.
prospect.medical: Two bulging discs in the lower back, MRI-confirmed. Original injury 2017-2018, re-aggravated in 2020 which is when the MRI was taken; completed a course of physical therapy which helped. Ongoing morning stiffness with limited forward flexion — 'I can like touch the middle of my shins and not like my feet' — which eases through the day. Attributes his stubborn waistline and lower-back fat partly to the injury and the sedentary job. No clinician currently involved and no clearance discussed.

signals: Lost ground over roughly five years to a hard season he names precisely — 'the injury and the relationship and the fact that I elevated in my profession. It's kind of like a three-headed storm there'
Wants a specific former self back — 'I used to have a six pack. I used to be really looking good and I don't have any abs anymore at all'
Carries visible self-directed regret — 'I can't stand what I look like in the mirror' and 'it's just stupid, stupid excuses, to be honest with you'
Post-breakup reset is an explicit driver — 'I recently got out of my relationship. So now like I'm really focused on myself'

Close to the_optimizer — 33, athletic base, clean nutrition, discipline, and no price resistance at all — but rejected because he has genuinely lost the condition rather than seeking incremental gain from a good baseline

goals.text: Get shredded again and get his six-pack back — 'Trying to get shredded again, for sure'
Lose the stubborn waistline and lower-back fat he cannot shift
Break a training plateau after ten to fifteen years of the same split
Become consistent for good rather than cycling — 'I'm really ready to prioritize fitness. I'm really ready to be disciplined again'
Collapse two hours of separate cardio and lifting into one 30-40 minute session
Train anywhere without being tied to a gym or a schedule — office to office, state to state, or on the beach
Improve mobility and morning stiffness around the disc injury
Look better in order to date again after the breakup — 'if I want to put myself out there, I want to look a little bit better'
Never end up like the rest of his family — 'I have a heavier set family... I don't want to ever get like that'
Eventually teach — wants to instruct yoga and possibly kettlebells: 'I do enjoy teaching others already'

pains.text: Plateaued on an unchanged routine — 'my routine hasn't changed in 10 years... Eventually, it stops because I'm doing the same thing'
Repeated relapse cycle — gets in shape for three or four months then falls off, including six-month gaps
Ten-hour desk days leave no room — 'I rose the ranks of my company so fast that I have so much responsibility now. I can't get out from under my desk'
Put health last behind work and his relationship — 'I felt like those were more important than my own fitness'
Two bulging lumbar discs and morning stiffness that cost him gym time for recovery
Evening gym is unusable and becomes the excuse — 'The gym is absolutely packed... And then I'm like, all right, I'll do it tomorrow. Like that's the problem'
Splitting cardio and lifting into two sessions a day was unsustainable — 'it was kind of a lot'
Fresh out of a three-year relationship and rebuilding around himself
Cannot stand his own reflection — 'dude, like, I can't stand what I look like in the mirror'
No idea how to start with kettlebells — 'I don't really work out with kettlebells, so I don't know like what to buy, like what weights to start with'

objections.raw_quote: Is that all paid at one time or is it, can it be like a monthly payment or anything like that?
objections.rep_response: Deflected to a credit card rather than disclosing that instalment plans and third-party financing exist: 'It just depends. A lot of our clients just throw it on a credit card and then figure out the payments of the back-end.' The prospect accepted it immediately — 'yeah, it still sounds good' — and paid in full on one card eight minutes later.

objections.raw_quote: So after the six months is done, I would lose access to school and, like, the other, like, I don't know if you have, like, video tutorials on how to do workouts or anything like that. Do you automatically get dropped off of the app after the six months?
objections.rep_response: Confirmed the limitation honestly but only after payment had been taken: 'So, I mean, generally, yes. But again, like, the whole goal is that by the time you're through it, you have so much repetition that you got it from there.'

evidence: Payment taken live on the call: 'Okay, I just put the payment through' followed by the rep confirming 'Yeah, there it is.'
Full $6,000 on a single credit card — 'I think I can do it all on one' — with the prospect confirming the amount afterwards: 'it kind of sucks that I had to put $6,000 down'.
Onboarding executed on the call: Trevor's 30-minute session booked for Wednesday at 7:15, onboarding form email received, Skool community walked through on screen.
Belief and commitment stated before the price: '10, easily. Trust me when I tell you that I'm all in right now.'

Counter-evidence, minor: the agreement was opened but never confirmed signed — 'I'm viewing it now. It says I need a sign' — and the Skool membership was left 'pending' with the rep messaging the team to approve it, so two onboarding steps closed unverified.
Counter-evidence, minor: the rep initially processed on faith — 'Dude, let's assume it went through for now. Until I see it here' — before confirming.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor booked for Wednesday 7:15pm; sign the agreement; Skool membership approval pending with the team; complete the onboarding form; weekly group workouts Thursdays 12:30 his time.

notable.note: The cleanest close in the batch and the only call where the commitment check ran before the price — a 1-to-10 belief question answered '10, easily' at 00:37:02, price at 00:38:34, paid at 00:46:21. But he disclosed two MRI-confirmed bulging lumbar discs, in passing and mid-sentence, and nobody asked whether a clinician had cleared him for loaded ballistic training. The rep instead used the injury as a selling point — 'we got a lot of guys that come to us with bulging discs, herniated discs, just back pain in general. And once we get them moving right again, it makes a huge impact.' Kettlebell swings and snatches load exactly the segment involved. He also asked a direct question about monthly payments and was steered to a credit card, on a day when the same rep walked two other prospects through Payvo and PayPal financing. And he learned that app and community access ends at six months only after he had paid.

quality.notes: Persistent short-turn swapping and several long inversions. The most consequential: the entire bulging-disc disclosure at 00:08:00 is labelled 'frankabt' but runs straight into the rep's follow-up question inside the same block, and the prospect's whole answer about plateauing is attributed across both labels; the rep's 'What type of work do you do?' at 00:01:46 appears inside a prospect block; and the price presentation at 00:38:34-00:39:12 alternates so that the rep's tiers and the prospect's payment question sit under the wrong names. Roles resolved from content. Height and weight were never established at any point despite fat loss being the primary goal, so those fields are null rather than estimated.
